CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA

ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Mallikarjun.B.Ryakha, learned counsel for the appellants who appeared before this Court physically as well as Sri.S.V.Hegde Mulkhand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 who appeared through video conference.

2. Dissatisfied with the amount that is awarded as compensation, the claimants are before this Court challenging the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru in MVC No.1492/2018 dated 27.04.2021.
As against the claim for NC: 2024:KHC:31881 Rs.10,00,000/-, the Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.2,10,000/- as compensation.

3. Arguing the matter, learned counsel Sri.Mallikarjun.B.Ryakha submits that the first appellant is the daughter and second appellant is the son of the deceased Lakshminarasamma (herein after referred to as deceased for brevity).
Both of them were residing with the deceased and were depending upon the earnings of the deceased by the date of accident.
The appellant No.1 is physically challenged by 80% and she was entirely depended upon the earnings of the deceased.
The appellants produced sufficient proof to show that they were living with the deceased and were depending upon her.
However, the Tribunal did not consider the said fact and awarded a meager sum as compensation.
4. Learned counsel also states that the deceased by doing agriculture and by selling vegetables was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- p.m. which NC: 2024:KHC:31881 is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel also states that the Miss Padma vs Hanumantharayappa on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192806770/

sentences.text: Tribunal deducted 50% towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, but as the dependents are two in number, such deduction should be 1/3rd as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Smt. sentences.text: Learned counsel thereby seeks enhancement of the compensation and grant the amount claimed.

5. Opposing the submission thus made, Sri.S.V.Hegde Mulkhand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 contends that deceased as per the evidence produced by the appellants themselves was aged about 77 years by the date of accident.

The second appellant being the major son and the first appellant being the daughter who attained the age of majority are at liability to look after the welfare of their mother i.e., the deceased and therefore, it cannot be held that the appellants were depending upon the income of the deceased by the date of accident.
NC: 2024:KHC:31881 Learned counsel also states that as the amount which is awarded as compensation is highly justifiable, the appeal is not maintainable.
6. A perusal of the records reveals absence of any substantive proof with regard to the exact occupation and income of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
However, there is an observation made by the Tribunal in the impugned order that the appellants were residing along with the deceased.
The submission made by the learned counsel for the appellants is that the first appellant being a physically challenged women was depending upon her mother for her livelihood.
It is not the case of the respondent as well that the deceased was suffering from any ailments by the date of accident.

Therefore, considering the fact that the appellants were residing with the deceased by the date of accident, this Court is of the view that the notional income of the deceased has to be taken as Rs.10,000/- p.m. NC: 2024:KHC:31881 7.

Though the learned counsel for the appellants argued that the Tribunal erred in deducting 50% of the earnings towards personal and living expenses yet this Court is of the view that the second claimant i.e., the son of the deceased who was aged about 39 years by the date of the accident cannot be held to be the dependent of the deceased.
Therefore, the deduction made towards personal and living expenses by the Tribunal cannot be interfered with.
The appropriate multiplier to be applied as observed by the Tribunal is 5.

Thus the loss of dependency if calculated will be as under:
Notional monthly income Rs.10,000/-

Annual income Rs.1,20,000/-
 Deducting 50% towards Rs.60,000/-

The Tribunal for the reasons best known has not awarded any amount towards loss of parental NC: 2024:KHC:31881 consortium.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is required to be awarded towards loss of parental consortium.

In the light of the forgoing discussion, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2024:KHC:31881 (ii) The compensation granted by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru through orders in MVC No.1492/2018 dated 27.04.2021 is enhanced from Rs.2,10,000/- to Rs.3,70,000/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw their respective shares.
(vi) The apportionment made and the order of pay and recovery remains undisturbed.
